title: Lighthouse guided quickwalk templates for first-time console setup
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: design a lightweight, persona-driven set of in-product onboarding "Lighthouse" templates that help first-time users complete core console tasks (create API key, run a sample inference, view cost preview, and set a rollout). These templates should combine short checklist steps, one-click starter templates, and an optional guided tour that can be dismissed.

Background: current empty states and first-run guidance are fragmented across the Console. Customers report uncertainty about where to start and how to evaluate cost/latency trade-offs quickly. This ticket bundles a small library of guided quickwalks for common personas (Individual dev, ML engineer, Platform admin) and a tiny interactive rollout simulator to help users understand canary vs full rollouts.

Design principles: 1) Minimal cognitive load — show exactly 3 next actions in each Lighthouse template. 2) Contextual learning — surface ephemeral tooltips tied to the active task, not global overlays. 3) Action-first — include prefilled templates and deep links (create project, provision key, run sample) so users can achieve 'first success' in under 5 minutes. 4) Cost transparency — include a concise preview card showing estimated monthly cost for the chosen starter config.

Constraints: must work in small viewports (responsive), accessible (keyboard-first and screenreader labels), and integrate with existing rollout feature flags (ENG dependency below).

Stakeholders: Product (Jesse Park), Eng (Aisha Patel), Growth (Samira Okoye), Research (Liam Fisher).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Three persona templates (Dev, ML Engineer, Platform Admin) with copy, checklist, and one-click starter actions.
2) Each template includes a cost-preview card that estimates immediate token spend and monthly projection.
3) Guided tour option that can be toggled per-user and dismissed permanently.
4) Empty-state placement for new workspaces that surfaces Lighthouse before other modules.
5) Accessibility: keyboard navigation + aria labels confirmed in QA checklist.
6) Usability test run with at least 8 participants and summary documented in the design folder.
deliverables: Design spec doc: copy, microcopy, checklist logic
Component tokens: sticker sheet for the cost-preview card
